message.reasoning:
I'm planning JUnit 4 tests for the Element class, mapping out key methods like constructors, ensureChildNodes, hasAttributes, attributes, tagName, attr, and parents to identify boundary cases and branch conditions to cover. I'm continuing to catalog the rest of Element's methods -- child, children, childElementsList, textNodes, dataNodes, select/is, appendChild and its variants, insertChildren, siblingElements, and cssSelector -- noting the null checks, index bounds, and conditional branches each test should exercise. Now I'm moving through more methods: getElementsByTag and related finders needing Validate.notEmpty, regex methods that catch PatternSyntaxException, text() and ownText() which use NodeVisitor logic checking for TextNode/Element instances and whitespace handling, and finally data(), className(), and classNames(). I'm continuing through the remaining pieces: classNames(Set), hasClass() with its length and whitespace scanning, addClass/removeClass/toggleClass, val() checking for textarea tags, outerHtmlHead/Tail with their pretty-print and self-closing conditions, html(), toString(), and the clone methods. This is a huge class, so I'm aiming to write a comprehensive test suite covering most of these with reasonable effort, focusing on branch coverage. I'll rely on Jsoup.parse and Element constructors being available on the test classpath since they compile together with the source under test, and organize tests methodically starting with constructor tests for tag strings and values. I'm planning coverage for null tag and base URI validation, attribute lazy initialization, base URI retrieval, empty child node sizing, tag name changes and empty-string errors, block detection, id and attribute value handling, boolean attributes, dataset access, parent traversal including null and hierarchical cases, and child index bounds checking. Continuing through children handling with mixed node types, text and data nodes, CSS selection including null results and query/evaluator checks, child node manipulation (append, prepend, insert with negative/out-of-bounds indices and varargs), element and text insertion, before/after positioning for strings and nodes, emptying content, wrapping, and CSS selector tests for id, class, and no-class cases. I'm now covering sibling element traversal (next, previous, first, last, with and without a parent, including null cases and sibling indices), followed by element lookup methods: by tag, by id, by class, and by attribute with various conditions (starting value, matching value, negated value, and value prefix matching). Then I'm testing more attribute-based lookups — containing, pattern-matching, and regex-based matching (including invalid regex error handling), plus index-based filters (less than, greater than, equals). The remaining tests cover text content matching — containing text, own text, pattern and regex matching for both, retrieving all elements, extracting full and own text, and checking whether an element has text. This is a huge list, so I'm scaling back my plan to a comprehensive but manageable set of maybe 60-70 tests covering class name handling, attribute/value manipulation, class add/remove/toggle, form value getting/setting, HTML retrieval and setting, string conversion, and cloning (both deep and shallow) -- enough for solid coverage without going overboard. Now I'm setting up imports for Jsoup, its DOM nodes, Elements, JUnit assertions, and regex support, planning to use Jsoup.parse for quick DOM construction in tests. I'm thinking through edge cases: testing that an invalid regex pattern in attribute matching throws appropriately, and that bounds-checking in insertChildren triggers an IllegalArgumentException via jsoup's Validate.isTrue. I'm recalling jsoup's Validate source—notNull and notEmpty also throw IllegalArgumentException—so my tests should expect that exception type consistently, and I'm also planning a cssSelector test for the nth-child branch when multiple siblings share a parent selection. I'm parsing two sibling `

` elements under a div and checking that the second element's cssSelector produces an nth-child qualifier, accounting for jsoup's automatic html/body wrapping affecting the parent chain. I'll set up a test parsing a div with two duplicate paragraph elements and compare their generated CSS selectors, checking that the second one includes an nth-child qualifier to distinguish it from the first. When there's only a single matching child, nth-child shouldn't be appended since the count is one. I need to check the id() branch too, prefixing with "#" when an id exists, and test cases with and without an id attribute set. For hasClass, I should also handle edge cases around class attribute length versus the expected class name length. Now I'm writing out the test cases for hasClass: checking a missing class attribute returns false, a shorter class string returns false, an exact-length case-insensitive match returns true, and scanning multiple space-separated classes correctly identifies matches in the middle and at the end while rejecting non-matches.
